title: Robustness of Cheap Defenses Under Adaptive vs Static Attacks

original_idea.body: Evaluate 2 cheap defenses against static then lightly-adaptive attacks (a rephrasing loop) and quantify how much apparent robustness drops.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying static-vs-adaptive robustness gap directly informs whether deployed defenses survive real attackers; defensible chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two cheap defenses + an adaptive rephrasing loop is guided engineering; novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but building the adaptive loop harness adds a workstream beyond static evaluation.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Reusable red-team harness, public attacks, no internal access; addresses an open problem labs deprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + small rephrasing loop on small models; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Static-vs-adaptive gap is a known pitfall; quantifying it for cheap defenses may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The static-vs-adaptive evaluation gap is documented; quantifying it for cheap deployable defenses may be open.
